title: Test-Time Search for Automated GFM Fine-Tuning

problem.claim: Adapting Graph Foundation Models to downstream tasks requires navigating an exponentially large decision space and traditionally demands substantial expert effort.

contributions.claim: GFMTuner automates Graph Foundation Model fine-tuning by combining Large Language Model agents with Monte Carlo Tree Search.
GFMTuner accepts natural-language task descriptions and generates fine-tuning strategies through test-time search.
The framework introduces a Graph-Instructed Actor with graph analysis tools and Gradient Consistency as a self-supervised reward for evaluating strategies.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across diverse graph domains, experiments reportedly show that GFMTuner matches or exceeds human expert designs.
The authors report reducing fine-tuning effort from weeks to a single natural-language query.
Code is reported as available in the linked GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph Foundation Models are transferable, but downstream adaptation involves a large decision space and heavy expert effort.
GFMTuner combines LLM agents with Monte Carlo Tree Search to automate fine-tuning.
The framework uses natural-language task descriptions to generate strategies through test-time search.
Graph analysis tools ground action generation, while Gradient Consistency provides a self-supervised strategy-evaluation reward.
Experiments reportedly match or exceed human expert designs while reducing effort, and code is available.

source_observation.claim: The framework uses test-time search with LLM agents and graph-specific analysis tools to generate fine-tuning strategies from natural-language task descriptions.

interpretation.claim: Search-based orchestration may reduce the expert burden of selecting among many adaptation decisions when task requirements can be expressed in language.

application.claim: A similar pattern could be considered for other configuration-heavy machine-learning adaptation workflows with domain-specific analysis tools.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach generalizes beyond the reported graph domains or under what task and compute constraints.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evaluated graph domains, datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the search budget, computational cost, or implementation details of the framework.
The abstract does not provide independent verification of the reported performance or effort reduction.
